cells.reason: The anchor is California's drinking-water MCL of 0.010 mg/L for water delivered by public water systems (Title 22 section 64431), a ug/L water standard; the regulation page states it 'is a drinking-water standard, not a food limit' and 'should not be compared directly to a food-occurrence concentration', and the protocol treats a drinking-water row as a different basis family from a food-content cell, so (b) fails regardless of scope. No sovereign hexavalent-chromium food-content ML exists in the register (its 19 Cr-VI rows are drinking water, toy migration, textiles, leather, RoHS, tattoo ink, metal adornments and fertilisers), so the nearest same-basis sovereign instruments are the parent-total chromium rows that bound the species (Cr-VI is at most total Cr): GB 2762-2025 Table 7 item 5.1 'Aquatic animals and their products' 2.0 mg/kg (china_gb2762_2025_crtotal_aquatic_animals_and_products_2000), whose 'and their products' wording reaches canned fish; Hong Kong Cap 132V 'Fish' total chromium 1000 (hk_cap132v_crtotal_fish_1000) would bind at 1000 if its food description is read to include canned fish, which the regulation page does not settle. A firm 10 ug/kg transposed from water is a manufactured number; the cell should be bounded by the parent total that certainly applies, 2000 (1000 if the HK 'Fish' description is confirmed to cover canned fish), disclosed as species-bounded, or carried as a disclosed baseline screen.
